sources.title: GTA 6 reinvigorates PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X console sales in the US, even at their inflated prices
sources.text: Despite the far higher prices of PlayStation and Xbox consoles today compared to their launch, or even the same period last year, both brands of console saw a significant boost in US sales leading up to the launch of this generation's biggest game: Grand Theft Auto 6. In the week ending 14th November, PS5 hardware unit sales registered a 2.4x increase over the same week last year. Xbox wasn't far behind, seeing a 2.3x increase in its own unit sales. That's according to industry analyst Mat Piscatella at Circana , who pulled the data from Circana's retail tracking service, which covers the US retail market. The PS5 Pro only accounted for less than 10 percent of the PlayStation's total unit sales, by the way, which Piscatella noted was "a LOT better than it has been in recent weeks", and seemingly the result of increased supply. GTA 6, of course, released on 19th November, so the surge in console hardware sales was clearly driven by the rush to attain consoles before the game came out. And while the GTA 6-driven demand isn't surprising, it's worth noting how much more expensive PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are today. A standard PS5 today costs $650, compared to $550 a year ago. The PS5 Pro saw a big jump from $750 last November to $900 today. The base Xbox Series X jumped from $650 last year to $800 today, while Series S now costs $500, up from $400. Even Switch 2, where GTA 6 is not available, saw a notable boost of 40 percent in hardware sales over the same period, driven by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and the special edition Zelda Switch 2 console . Circana's November US video game market report, which releases in December, is already one of the most anticipated this year, for digesting and documenting the GTA 6 effect. Worldwide, GTA 6 sold more than 32.5m copies in one day , making Rockstar's parent company Take-Two $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue. We haven't had any updated official sales figures since; but estimates suggest the sales figure could be well into the 40-millions. Perhaps Rockstar is waiting to hit the nice round 50m sales mark before announcing it. If you're playing GTA 6, you may want to keep Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough to hand. It has plenty of very helpful guides covering the game's main missions, as well as explainers for mechanics like romance and the criminal profile , and even cheats for when you finish the game.

sources.text: Yank out ATMs and grab the cash with Yasmani's tips. Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash. There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above shows a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch. If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town. You can also get a winched truck around the back of Yasmani's vape shop in Little Cuba—the fence who gives you the ATM tip offs. You'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck. sources.title: GTA 6: All Secret Radio Stations and how to unlock them
sources.text: Unlock the secret radio and on-demand services in Grand Theft Auto 6 Grand Theft Auto 6 is hiding not just one, but two radio stations that you can easily play the whole game without finding. The Vault and The Sniper of LaPerle are two exclusive music playlists you can only listen to if you scan carefully placed posters around the world of GTA 6, and one of them even belongs to Kodak Black. For everything you need to unlock all secret radio stations in Grand Theft Auto 6 , read through the guide below. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To unlock The Vault as a radio station you can listen to pretty much anywhere, you need to visit the club, also called The Vault. Itâs in the center of Vice City, a block West of Nine1Nine. It has a unique icon, so itâs hard to miss. As you enter and go up the first flight of stairs, youâll see two posters in front of you. Scan the The Vault poster with the WAiNK App, and once complete, youâll unlock The Vault as a radio station you can listen to in your car. It plays the same kind of club and dance music youâll hear inside the club. The Sniper of LaPerle radio station is unlocked similarly to The Vault, but instead of scanning just one poster, you need to find four scattered around the LaPerle district of Vice City. This on-demand radio playlist is from the real-worldâs Kodak Black. A poster can be found inside the Drip Drops clothing store on the front desk. This location also serves as a front for San4San. Another can be found inside Twa Ponya Tattoo, just on the right as you walk in, on a small table next to the door. Head to Aunt Zolaâs Soul Food, Southwest of Tyroneâs place, and you can find a poster on the left wall inside. The last isnât in LaPerle; itâs inside Boobieâs strip club, the Jack of Hearts. Youâll need to progress to Chapter 3 in order to be let upstairs into the clubâs recording booth, where youâll usually find DreâQuan. The poster is on a case here. Once youâve found and scanned all four posters, youâll be able to listen to The Sniper of LaPerleâs on-demand mixtape from most in-game radios.

sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 features over 500 vehicles for you to get behind the wheel of, and whilst most of them are cars, there’s an incredible selection of motorcycles to pick from as well, and a ton of them know how to test the speed limits. Whether you’re racing through the streets of Vice City or simply looking for the perfect getaway vehicle, speed is always going to come in handy. Thankfully, of the nearly 80 motorcycles in the game, a lot of them are incredibly high-performance, though finding them can be a bit tricky. With that in mind, here are the 10 fastest motorcycles in GTA 6, as well as how you can get your hands on each one. You can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you haven’t already! The fastest motorcycle in Grand Theft Auto 6 is the Principe Burnished Alvino. This is one of the many Standout Vehicles in GTA 6, with the Principe Alvino being the base model of the motorcycle. But if you’re looking for speed on two wheels, you’ll find no better than the Principe Burnished Alvino. The best part about this motorcycle, though, is that it’s pretty easy to get a hold of, with no Trackers to deal with or Key Cloners necessary to take control. Better yet, it’s pretty cheap to register, too! But where do you find it? Find out further below. Of all the 77 motorcycles to be found in Grand Theft Auto 6, the ones listed below are the 10 fastest, strictly according to the in-game Speed stat. And of these 10 vehicles, five of them are Standouts, meaning you’ll have to go hunting in specific locations if you want to get your hands on them—but more on that later. For now, check out the complete table for the 10 fastest motorcycles in GTA 6: It’s all well and good knowing what the 10 fastest motorcycles are in Grand Theft Auto 6, but the real question is: how do you get your hands on them for yourself? Luckily for you, we have all of the answers. Below you’ll find the locations for all 10 of the motorcycles mentioned in the table above. You’ll find the Principe Burnished Alvino parked on Starfish Island. Head to the exact location marked on the maps above, and it’ll be there tucked away in a garage on the property—just beware of the security on the island. Getting a hold of Emilio’s Lectro is as easy as going to the location marked on the maps above and breaking into the garage. Since it’s on an open street, beware of becoming Wanted for trespassing, but the bike should make for a perfect getaway vehicle if you do. If you’re looking to acquire a Nagasaki SFB 1000 and want to find one reliably, your best bet is to grab the Standout version of the motorcycle, which can be found below, since the vehicle has a chance of spawning in a variety of places across Leonida. In order to get the Nagasaki KD’s SFB 1000, you’ll need to complete “Dre’Quan’s Gift,” a mission in GTA 6. This should become available partly through Chapter 3, sometime after the Photo/Shoot mission. Getting hold of the Nagasaki Smokescreen Carbon RS will have to wait until Chapter 3, as you need the Cut-Off Tool in order to break into a Scoop container. That said, if you have the equipment, head to the construction site marked on the map above, and use one of the nearby vehicles to move some concrete out of the way that’s blocking the entrance to the container. Inside, you’ll find the bike ready to go, and you’ll need it too, as there’s a chance you’ll be Wanted for trespassing. As is often the case with base versions of vehicles, it’s difficult to find a guaranteed spawn location, but we had very good spawn rates in the location marked above. Lots of bikes spawn in and around here, so check back a few times and see if one manages to spawn—you might even find one of the other base vehicles on this list, too! That said, you’re better off grabbing the Principe Burnished Alvino, the Standout version that’s also the fastest motorcycle in the game! The Nagasaki Hung Carbon RS can be found swinging from a tree just north of Belville. If you shoot the two rope points on the tree, the vehicle will drop down to the ground, where it will be unlocked and ready to roll. There’s no guaranteed spawn for the standard version of this vehicle, but the location marked above (the same as the Principe Alvino V1) proved particularly reliable during our testing. Several bikes can appear in this area, so keep an eye out and revisit if necessary. That said, you’re better off grabbing the Nagasaki Hung Carbon, the Standout version found in the entry above. Base versions of vehicles can be tricky to track down, as they don’t always have a guaranteed spawn location. Your best bet is to grab the Principe Emilio’s Lectro instead, which is the Standout variant featured in the second entry above. It’s also considerably faster, making it the better option all around! Finding a standard version of this vehicle can be a bit of a lottery, but we had plenty of luck at the location marked above. There are several bikes that spawn in this area, including the Principe Alvano V1 and the Nagasaki Carbon RS, so it’s worth checking back a few times if you don’t find one straight away. sources.text: A Black Friday 2026 acontece nesta sexta (27) e promete boas oportunidades para quem deseja comprar um teclado gamer novo. Mas, claro, é importante conhecer as principais características dos periféricos antes de aproveitar os descontos. Entre as opções disponíveis no mercado, há modelos mecânicos, ópticos e magnéticos, cada um com tecnologias e recursos diferentes. Tamanho, tipo de switch e possibilidades de personalização também podem impactar na sua escolha. Para te ajudar nessa tarefa, o VOXL reuniu dicas com base nas recomendações da equipe especializada da Pichau. Portanto, confira o que avaliar antes de investir em um teclado gamer e conheça opções para diferentes orçamentos. A principal diferença entre os teclados está na tecnologia utilizada para registrar o pressionamento das teclas. Os modelos magnéticos, mecânicos, ópticos e de membrana funcionam de maneiras distintas, o que afeta a velocidade de resposta, a sensação durante a digitação e até as possibilidades de personalização. Nos teclados magnéticos , por exemplo, cada switch utiliza um pequeno ímã acompanhado por sensores que identificam o movimento da tecla ao longo de todo o percurso. Como o registro acontece sem contato físico entre as peças, a tecnologia reduz o desgaste e permite ajustar o ponto de atuação por meio de um software. Já os modelos mecânicos tradicionais funcionam com o contato entre componentes internos para registrar o comando em um ponto específico. Eles oferecem diferentes tipos de switches, com variações de resistência, resposta tátil e ruído, além de opções para diferentes faixas de preço. Os teclados ópticos utilizam luz infravermelha para detectar o pressionamento, também sem depender de contato físico, mas sem acompanhar o curso completo da tecla como os magnéticos. Por fim, os teclados de membrana utilizam camadas de plástico para registrar os comandos e costumam ser encontrados em modelos mais acessíveis. São alternativas comuns para tarefas básicas e uso cotidiano, mas geralmente oferecem uma resposta menos rápida em comparação com as tecnologias mecânicas, ópticas e magnéticas. Para quem joga títulos competitivos, especialmente games de tiro em primeira pessoa (FPS), recursos de desempenho podem fazer diferença. Um deles é o ponto de atuação ajustável, que permite definir a profundidade necessária para registrar cada tecla, deixando o acionamento mais sensível ou exigindo um pressionamento maior para evitar comandos acidentais. Outro recurso presente em teclados magnéticos é o Rapid Trigger. Em modelos convencionais, a tecla precisa retornar a uma altura predeterminada antes de registrar um novo comando. Com essa tecnologia, o acionamento pode acontecer assim que o usuário começa a soltar a tecla, permitindo respostas mais rápidas em movimentos repetidos. O tamanho do teclado também merece atenção. Os modelos Full Size mantêm o bloco numérico, enquanto os TKL eliminam essa parte para liberar espaço. Já os formatos 65% e 75% oferecem opções compactas que preservam as setas direcionais, enquanto as opções de 60% são ainda menores e não contam com setas ou teclas de função dedicadas — que podem ser acessadas por atalhos. Outro ponto é conferir se o teclado oferece um software para criar perfis configuráveis, que geralmente permitem alternar entre ajustes de resposta para jogos e configurações mais confortáveis para atividades de trabalho ou estudo. Antes de fechar a compra, vale considerar como o teclado será utilizado no dia a dia. Quem trabalha com planilhas, por exemplo, pode preferir um modelo com teclado numérico, enquanto jogadores que precisam de mais espaço para movimentar o mouse podem aproveitar melhor as versões TKL ou compactas. Também é importante conferir a compatibilidade do layout e dos switches com suas preferências. Felizmente, há opções para todos os gostos e diferentes faixas de preços na Black Friday da Pichau. sources.title: Como escolher um monitor gamer na Black Friday 2026? Veja dicas do que avaliar
sources.text: Falta pouco para a Black Friday 2026, que acontece nesta sexta-feira (27) e promete boas oportunidades para quem deseja comprar um monitor gamer novo. A data pode ser uma boa chance de renovar o setup e encontrar telas de qualidade por preços mais acessíveis. Antes de aproveitar as ofertas, porém, é importante conhecer algumas características técnicas dos monitores. Taxa de atualização, tempo de resposta, resolução e até o tipo de painel são alguns dos fatores que influenciam diretamente na sua experiência de uso. Para ajudar nessa escolha, o VOXL reuniu algumas dicas de ouro com base nas recomendações da equipe especializada da Pichau — uma das maiores lojas de e-commerce gamer da América Latina. Confira abaixo o que avaliar antes de investir em um novo monitor e conheça opções para diferentes faixas de preço. O tipo de painel é um dos primeiros pontos que devem ser considerados na hora de escolher um monitor gamer, já que influencia a qualidade das cores, o contraste e a velocidade de resposta da tela. Entre as opções mais comuns do mercado estão os modelos TN, IPS e VA — e cada uma dessas opções possuem suas próprias características. Os painéis TN (Twisted Nematic) costumam priorizar velocidade e custo-benefício, oferecendo tempos de resposta que podem variar de 1 ms a 2 ms. Por isso, são uma boa alternativa para quem joga títulos competitivos como Valorant e Counter-Strike 2 — embora apresentem limitações na reprodução de cores e nos ângulos de visão. Enquanto isso, os modelos IPS (In-Plane Switching) oferecem cores mais precisas e ângulos de visão amplos, sendo interessantes tanto para jogos com foco em qualidade visual quanto para atividades como edição de vídeos e design. Nesse caso, vale observar também a cobertura de cores — indicada por padrões como sRGB e DCI-P3. Já os painéis VA (Vertical Alignment) , por sua vez, se destacam pelo contraste elevado e pela reprodução de tons de preto mais profundos. A combinação faz desse tipo de monitor uma opção bastante versátil para quem joga ou assiste filmes e faz outras atividades, especialmente em ambientes com pouca iluminação. Outro cuidado importante é equilibrar a resolução do monitor com a capacidade do computador. Telas 4K oferecem imagens mais detalhadas, embora exijam mais da placa de vídeo e do processador do seu PC. Por conta disso, antes de investir em um modelo com resolução elevada, vale conferir se o restante do setup aguenta o tranco. A taxa de atualização, que é medida em Hertz (Hz), também merece uma atenção especial. Para quem busca maior fluidez em jogos competitivos, a recomendação é procurar monitores a partir de 144 Hz combinados com um tempo de resposta baixo para reduzir efeitos como o ghosting, que deixa rastros durante movimentos rápidos. Tecnologias de sincronização, como FreeSync e G-Sync, também podem fazer diferença no seu gameplay. Elas ajudam bastante a evitar a quebra de quadros, conhecida como screen tearing, ao sincronizar a taxa de atualização do monitor com a quantidade de quadros produzidos pela GPU. Por fim, não deixe a ergonomia e as conexões de lado. Recursos como Flicker Free, que reduz a cintilação da tela, e Low Blue Light, que diminui a emissão de luz azul, podem ser úteis para quem passa horas e horas na frente do computador. Além disso, para aqueles que querem economizar espaço na mesa, também vale conferir se o monitor conta com suporte ao padrão VESA — item necessário para utilizar braços articulados. Além de avaliar as especificações, é importante considerar o tamanho da tela e a distância entre o monitor e a cadeira. Um modelo maior nem sempre é a melhor escolha para qualquer bancada, especialmente quando a resolução não acompanha as dimensões do display. A equipe da Pichau também separou algumas opções de monitores gamer para diferentes orçamentos, com descontos que podem chegar a 40% durante a Black Friday. sources.title: Rockstar Explains Why it Added Consequences to GTA 6's Violence and Crimes
sources.text: Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6 . In an interview with Eurogamer , Nelson was asked about Rockstar's approach to the systems and themes in GTA 6. He said that a lot of it was born out of all of the work they put into Red Dead Redemption 2, specifically having a reactive world that responds to the player's behavior and choices. He explained that there was a desire to evolve the GTA experience and to "give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun.'" That means players can now point a gun at someone and threaten them, rather than having to beat or kill them to steal their money. The threat of violence is just as prevalent as the violence itself in GTA 6, and it also plays into the morality-adjacent system that is your criminal profile. The game doesn't explicitly punish you for doing bad things, because it's GTA, and you're bound to do bad things. However, it judges you on how harsh you are. If you rob a store with minimal force or only attack people if they draw on you first, attempting to minimize casualties, your profile won't change. If you go in and kill everyone, the level may decrease. This prompted Rockstar to expand NPC interactions even further. If you drew a gun in GTA 5, no one cared until it was actively pointed at them. Now, people will begin to quietly scurry away if they see you pull a rifle out of your trunk. Nelson explained that while the powerful rampages were fun for a while in previous games, they lacked substance and would get old quickly. In GTA 6, the process to start mowing people down takes a bit more thought because you don't have an endless pocket of weapons anymore. "You have to call your car," says Nelson. "You have to pop a car trunk and get [a weapon], and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up, and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them. "And then, you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off, and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your criminal profile until it breaks, and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'" The more realistic approach with GTA 6 has been a bit divisive for purists. Some don't want consequences; they want a power fantasy, and GTA 6 is decidely not that. If you want a supercar, it's going to take you dozens of hours before you can steal one. There's a progression to the chaos. For some, that's more rewarding. For others who want that quick fix, it's cumbersome. It'll be interesting to see how Rockstar looks at all of the responses to the game and how that informs the next GTA. Will they go further down this path or will they try to find a greater middle ground? The game certainly isn't hurting despite some vocal critics. GTA 6 is the highest rated game in history on Metacritic and generated nearly $4 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours , making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. IGN gave the game a 10 out of 10 , praising it for its depth and detail. "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from our review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played." Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
sources.text: You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to. Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie. But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC . “As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?” When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.” I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage. That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. There’s a world of possibilities out there. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map . sources.title: GTA 6 The Missing Link Walkthrough
sources.text: How to complete The Missing Link and what to do with Monty How to complete The Missing Link in GTA 6. The Missing Link is a main story mission in GTA 6 that sees Lucia and Andrea attempt to capture a senior cartel member named Monty. In this The Missing Link walkthrough, we’ll explain how to finish the mission, how to get the unique weapon from this mission, and what you should do with Monty at the end of the mission. Over the last week we’ve published dozens of GTA 6 Guides. We’re about to enter Chapter 4 in our complete GTA 6 walkthrough. Check it our in our GTA 6 walkthrough hub.Â Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To unlock The Missing Link, you first need to complete the Company Property mission in Chapter 3. Once it’s available, travel to Sloppy Molly’s in Watson Bay as Lucia. Make sure you’re playing as Lucia alone, as Andrea is waiting to meet her there. Head to Sloppy Molly’s and meet Andrea. After the introductory conversation, Lucia changes clothes and follows Andrea across the street into a warehouse hosting an illegal cockfight. You don’t have to take part in this thankfully, just stand around until the next part of the mission starts. Wait for Andrea to receive a message from her contact. When prompted, head to the entrance beside the bouncer wearing a white suit. Follow Andrea through the building until you reach Monty in a back room. Monty is a senior Cartel enforcer that Lucia and Andrea are targetting. Monty asks Lucia and Andrea to pose for photographs intended for the cartel’s social media accounts. Enter the back room and follow the on-screen prompts to change poses and take the required pictures. It doesn’t matter what you do in this section, as long as you take the pictures, the mission will continue. Unfortunately, the meeting soon turns violent. You’ll need to fight Monty using melee attacks until he is knocked unconscious. Once Monty is down, enemy gang members arrive and you’ll need to clear a path for Andrea. Take cover whenever possible and watch the doorways for incoming enemies. Continue fighting through the warehouse, paying particular attention to the large cockfighting room. Additional enemies arrive through the garage entrance on the right. Once the building is clear, Andrea and Lucia take Monty outside and put him in the boot of a car. Get into the vehicle and follow the GPS towards Vice City. Gang members will pursue you, but you should lose them after leaving Hamlet. Partway through the journey, you’ll be prompted to switch characters and take control of Jason. The game will now switch to Jason. As Jason, head to the front of the building and meet Lucia and Andrea. Open the boot, pull Monty out and escort him towards the backyard at gunpoint. When Raul gives the instruction, knock Monty down. You’ll then need to operate a loader to suspend Monty over an alligator-filled pool while Raul questions him. Follow Raul’s instructions carefully, raising and lowering Monty as required. Don’t lower him completely into the water, as this will kill him and prevent you from earning the Professional bonus. Once Raul has finished questioning Monty, you’ll be given the choice to put him back on dry land or drop him into the alligator pool. Both options complete the mission, so the final decision is yours. If you want to get the professional bonus for this mission, you can’t kill Monty. You can complete the mission without killing Monty, you just need to continue to interrogate him. Monty’s pistol is an optional weapon pickup during The Missing Link. After knocking out Monty and defeating the first enemy during the warehouse shootout,Â spin back toward where you came from and return to the photo room. You’ll find the pistol lying on the floor next to him. Make sure you collect it before progressing through the warehouse, as you won’t get another opportunity to pick it up during the mission. You also can’t reenter this area once the mission is finished, making this weapon missable. As mentioned the previous section, you can acquire a unique weapon during an early portion of the mission, which is the main reward. That’s everything you need to know to complete The Missing Link in GTA 6.

sources.text: Todos disponíveis a partir de 1 de dezembro. Mande ver nos corrimãos, enfrente ícones e fuja de horrores além da compreensão com os Jogos Mensais PlayStation Plus de dezembro. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 e Amnesia: The Bunker ficam disponíveis para todos os assinantes do PlayStation Plus* de terça-feira, 1º de dezembro, até segunda-feira, 4 de janeiro. Vamos conhecer um pouco mais sobre cada jogo. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 – Edição Cross-Gen | PS5, PS4 Avise a vizinhança e chame a galera do skate, porque a manobra não morreu: a clássica franquia volta com Tony Hawk’s™ Pro Skater™ 3 + 4. Tudo o que você curtia está de volta e repaginado, com mais skatistas, pistas novas, manobras mais pesadas, trilha sonora no volume máximo e muito mais. Caia nas pistas novas ou detone pelos cenários clássicos de Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 e Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 4, recriados em 4K**, com objetivos mais diretos e o clássico formato de 2 minutos. Jogue do seu jeito nos modos expandidos Criar um Skatista e Criar um Parque, agora com a opção inédita de criar objetivos personalizados para compartilhar com os amigos. Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 entrega uma experiência completa de Dragon Ball, com muita ação, batalhas intensas e diversas opções de personalização. Crie seu personagem, explore Conton City e treine com mestres icônicos da série para enfrentar inimigos poderosos e proteger o fluxo da História. Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 também traz modos multijogador online para enfrentar jogadores do mundo todo ou entrar em Batalhas de Invasão contra inimigos gigantes em equipe. Amnesia: The Bunker é um jogo de terror em primeira pessoa dos criadores de Soma e Amnesia. Sozinho em um bunker abandonado da Primeira Guerra Mundial, com apenas uma bala no tambor, você precisa encarar os horrores que espreitam no escuro. Descubra várias maneiras de sobreviver lá dentro. Na pele do soldado francês Henri Clément, você conta com um revólver, uma lanterna de dínamo barulhenta e poucos suprimentos para coletar e criar itens pelo caminho. Com elementos aleatórios e comportamento imprevisível, nenhuma partida é igual à outra. Caçado por uma ameaça constante que reage a cada passo e som, você precisa adaptar seu estilo de jogo para sobreviver a esse inferno. Cada decisão muda a forma como o jogo reage. Toda ação tem consequência. Última chance para adicionar os Jogos Mensais PlayStation Plus de novembro Assinantes PlayStation Plus têm até segunda-feira, 30 de novembro, para adicionar os Jogos Mensais de novembro à biblioteca: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV – VI Remastered e Monster Train 2. *A seleção PlayStation Plus pode variar de acordo com a região. Consulte PlayStation.com para mais detalhes. **A versão de PS5 roda em 4K nativo a 60 FPS no modo Fidelidade. A saída 4K exige um dispositivo ou tela compatível com 4K.

sources.text: A Sony revelou nesta quinta-feira (26) a lista de jogos mensais do PlayStation Plus para dezembro de 2026. Os assinantes do serviço poderão resgatar três novos títulos, que incluem experiências de esporte, ação e terror. Os jogos estarão disponíveis a partir da próxima terça-feira (1º) para assinantes de todos os planos do serviço: Essential, Extra e Deluxe. O prazo para adicioná-los à biblioteca termina em 4 de janeiro de 2027. A clássica franquia de skate retorna com versões recriadas dos cenários de Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 e 4, gráficos em 4K, pistas inéditas e o tradicional formato de sessões de dois minutos. O título também amplia a seleção de skatistas e os modos de personalização de personagens e pistas, permitindo que os jogadores desenvolvam objetivos personalizados e compartilhem suas criações com amigos. Baseado na franquia criada por Akira Toriyama, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 permite que os jogadores criem seus próprios personagens, explorem Conton City e treinem com figuras icônicas do anime para proteger a linha do tempo da série. Além da campanha, o título oferece modalidades multijogador online e batalhas cooperativas contra inimigos gigantes. Desenvolvido pela Frictional Games, responsável por Soma e pela franquia Amnesia, o jogo de terror em primeira pessoa acompanha Henri Clément, um soldado francês preso em um bunker abandonado durante a Primeira Guerra Mundial. Com recursos limitados, o jogador precisa administrar seus equipamentos, explorar o ambiente e adaptar suas estratégias para sobreviver a uma criatura que reage aos sons e movimentos realizados durante a partida. Os assinantes do PlayStation Plus têm até segunda-feira (30) para adicionar os jogos mensais de novembro à biblioteca. São eles: Os jogos mensais resgatados permanecem disponíveis na biblioteca dos jogadores enquanto a assinatura do PlayStation Plus estiver ativa. Amazon Prime também é feito para jogadores! sources.title: Staff at Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar vote against union recognition deal
sources.text: Workers at Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar Games have voted against a union recognition deal. 1,544 staff members took part in the vote across the company's locations in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London, representing a 93.2% turnout. Despite this huge engagement, 75.3% voted against Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) union recognition, while 24.7% voted in favour. Had this vote gone the other way, IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union would have been the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry, and Rockstar would have been obligated to engage with collective bargaining on pay and working hours. "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6," the company's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said in a statement. "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together," said a company rep. IWGB says that Rockstar staff will keep organising regardless of whether the union is formally recognised. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for," the organisation said in its own statement. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen. "Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us. "A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs. "The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands." Under UK law, the union may not re-apply for recognition for three years, although staff remain free to join the RGWU. The question of forming a union at Rockstar Games followed allegations that 34 members of staff were let go from the Grand Theft Auto maker in a move that IWGB called union-busting . Rockstar parent company Take-Two has denied this claim, saying that staff were fired for "distributing and discussing confidential information". Rockstar and IWGB are currently embroiled in an employment tribunal regarding these job cuts; closing arguments were issued on November 19 . Judge Lucy Wiseman, who oversaw proceedings, said that there is no timeframe yet for the judgement, but said she would try her best to "get that judgement out as quickly as possible". Grand Theft Auto 6 launched on November 19th and made a record $3.79 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours on sale .

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: GTA 6's best lore drops happen when you're chilling with your partner, so stop leaving them at home all the time
sources.text: Learning things about your partner by spending time with them? Say it ain't so. My real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6 . I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do. And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments. Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful. But then, occasionally, beyond all the comedic conversations and flavour dialogue that give these characters so much life, the game'll drop some proper good lore. I'll do my best not to spoil stuff here, but for almost every complaint I've seen on social media about why certain protagonists did certain things, there's an answer tucked away in these interactions. The kind of things you'd really want to know about these characters? Your best chance of finding it all out is when you bring them together. I've really enjoyed having lore drops unfold in mundane conversations while walking around, driving, or eating a burger, rather than hamfisted into the main story. They feel like natural breathing moments for the couple to recount the past, or get into the stuff that was happening in the time that they were apart. You know, the exact kind of times actual couples and friends would find the time to dig into these things in real life, too. That doesn't mean you have to keep them together all the time. Some of their exclusive missions also provide a great bit of insight into their backstories—like Jason's side stuff with ex-army pal Bret Vogel, or the missions that have Lucia in some all-too-real situations with her mother. I've played plenty of the game flying solo as both protagonists too, and you'll occasionally get some of this nattering just by hanging around in your abode together. But I can't recommend enough that you find plenty of opportunities to bring them together out in the open world. Even if it's just for 15 minutes here and there, you'll uncover a whole lot about who they were before we first got to know them as the player. And as someone who has really enjoyed learning just about everything about these two as I can, it's been one of my favourite parts of the game so far. sources.title: The 14 Best Star Wars Games of All Time, Ranked
sources.text: Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium, encompassing everything from role-playing games and first-person shooters to arcade racers and XCOM clones (the latter of two seeing well-regard releases just this year). No matter the year or the hardware, some of the best Star Wars games are worth revisiting. Here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time, ranked. Play it on: PlayStation 4, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X People like Star Wars for different reasons, from the hero’s journey, to the beautiful planet environments and the thrilling space battles. A lot of the best Star Wars games tend to narrow their scope rather than focusing on everything at once, and Squadrons definitely prioritized at shootouts in the vast reaches of space. It dropped players in cockpits that might have featured in the original movies and let players feel like they were in the middle of an operation… especially when they had a VR headset equipped. The online component was initially another compelling reason to play, but activity levels have dropped off in the years since launch. Still, it has a lot to offer if you don’t mind a more solitary experience. Play it on: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X Respawn Entertainment has had multiple chances to do Star Wars justice, starting with this first entry in the Star Wars Jedi series. It introduces Cal Kestis, a hero living through the dark period following Revenge of the Sith . Not everyone loves the Jedi, even at the best of times. They feel a bit like the galaxy’s superheroes, and yet there’s no denying the thrill of a good lightsaber duel. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order focuses on that aspect in particular, and lets players explore interesting environments other games only allow them to glimpse from afar. It’s pretty and fun, despite performance issues at launch and some tedious backtracking. Play it on: PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X If you’re going to build a strategy game to entertain audiences in a post- XCOM world, you can do a lot worse for inspiration. Star Wars Zero Company took some winning elements from that venerated franchise and transported them to a galaxy far, far away. The result is one of the greatest Star Wars games ever created, featuring compelling turn-based combat and a generally satisfying plot centered in the Clone Wars era. Some players felt the exploration segments between battles introduced unwelcome filler. And the battles themselves sometimes were a little too easy to maintain tension. But such faults, as well as technical issues at launch that included camera issues and performance drops, were minor blemishes on an otherwise standout experience that leaves us hoping for a similarly spectacular sequel. Play it on: PlayStation 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox Following closely after Star Wars: Starfighter , which released one year prior, Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter added Force abilities that proved devastating in space battles. The arsenal of weapons expanded, plus a full split-screen cooperative campaign added a new dimension to the experience. Critics at the time weren’t impressed by how much of the experience felt like the previous game, though, and the disjointed storyline couldn’t match what came before it. Even so, it served as a worthy follow-up and was better than its predecessor in some key ways. Jedi Starfighter is easy to play on a PlayStation 4 , as well, despite the date of its original release. When word first arrived that BioWare was working on another Star Wars RPG set in the Old Republic, visions of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic danced in our heads. However, we eventually learned that Star Wars: The Old Republic would actually take the form of an MMORPG, which dulled some of that early enthusiasm. Fortunately, the game turned out much better than it easily might have, even if it did sometimes feel like World of Warcraft in disguise and initially lacked a meaningful endgame. When early subscription numbers faltered, Electronic Arts explored a free-to-play model, allowing it to build the following it needed to justify continued development. Since then, the game has seen additional content drops, even after Disney’s acquisition of Lucasfilm. If you are so inclined, you can experience much of that content for free, thanks to the ongoing stewardship of Broadsword Online Games. Play it on: Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X Lego Star Wars was a surprise hit when it arrived for PlayStation 2. A variety of sequels since then have also proven to be great fun. The Skywalker Saga is the biggest release of the lot, presenting a fresh take on the stories in all nine movies about the Skywalker family and their friends. Rather than compiling and touching up everything that came before (which is partly contained in Lego Star Wars: The Complete Saga ), it presents the classic stories with a thoroughly modern touch. Some of the older elements, like a fixed camera and confusing level progression, have been cleaned up for the 2022 release. The much larger and more complex level hubs are also a satisfying development. Such improvements make The Skywalker Saga the definitive way to see your favorite Star Wars heroes doing heroic things in plastic brick form. The game is also a terrific option if you’re looking for something you can play with your less experienced friends or even small children, as one might expect from the Lego games, though the second player sometimes must take a back seat while the main hero does the tricky stuff. sources.title: Unreal Engine 6 won't include Blueprints or Actor Gameplay Framework
sources.text: EVP of Development says Epic expects using AI will make converting projects from UE5 to UE6 more "practical and cost-efficient" Unreal Engine 6 will discontinue support for Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework, instead utilising Verse and Epic's new Scene Graph framework. In a blog post, Marcus Wassmer, EVP of Development, acknowledged this change contradicts Epic Games' June announcement that Blueprints and Actors "would coexist in UE6 Early Access and 6.0, so UE projects could upgrade incrementally while the new Scene Graph framework matures." "However, with recent advances in AI capability, we expect AI to massively help with converting UE5 projects to UE6, if not make that process fully automatic. That also means we can deliver UE6 on time (or sooner) while meeting its design goals: a new data model, a Verse-first architecture, modularity, and AI operability." Wassmer stated that Epic expects AI will make converting projects from UE5 to UE6 more "practical and cost efficient." "The cost of any given task with AI has been going down 13x year over year, and the complexity of converting a game remains more or less constant," said Wassmer. "We expect this trend to continue and to accelerate, which should result in modest conversion costs by the time UE 6.0 is out in the world." "Fortnite has one of the largest libraries of Blueprints anywhere. Two weeks ago, we experimented with using AI to convert all of the Blueprints for Battle Royale to Verse. This project was expected to take years, but we now have a working prototype of Fortnite that is about 3 million lines of Verse code after porting more than 20,000 Blueprints. Wassmer concluded: "The team is hard at work iterating to validate the resulting performance, memory usage, and architecture. We’re doing this at scale now, and this conversion will help make the process as easy as possible for everyone else." The latest build of Unreal Engine is scheduled for 2027 and recently entered preview ahead of the Epic AI MegaJam. UE 5.9 will introduce several UE6 AI tools, including expanded Python scripting, Model Context Protocol (MCP) improvements, browser deployment capabilities, and the shared workspace Unreal Canvas .
